ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a benzene ring, with a segment of side chain connected to the right side of the benzene ring; the side chain connects from the benzene ring to the benzylic carbon, then connects to the nitrogen marked with a positive charge. The nitrogen is also connected to three carbon substituents. There are also curved arrows and charge symbols in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring arrows and not counting hydrogen-related bonds. Counting by fragments: around the benzene ring there are 6 C–C bonds; from the benzene ring to the benzylic carbon, and then from the benzylic carbon to nitrogen, there are 2 heavy-atom bonds; from nitrogen to the three carbon substituents there are 3 N–C bonds. The total is 6 + 2 + 3 = 11.

raw_record.question_text: In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen. Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Count bonds fragment by fragment. First count the six C–C bonds around the benzene ring. Then count the two heavy-atom bonds in the side chain from the ring to the benzylic carbon and from that carbon to nitrogen. Finally count the three N–C bonds from nitrogen to its three substituents. Do not count hydrogens, curved arrows, or isolated charge/counterion symbols. Sum 6 + 2 + 3 = 11.

method.method_draft: Make a bond-order inventory. From the benzene ring, record 3 double bonds and 3 single bonds. Outside the ring, record 5 more single bonds: ring-to-benzylic carbon, benzylic carbon-to-N, and three N–carbon substituent bonds. Record 0 triple bonds. Total bonds = double-bond items 3 + single-bond items (3 + 5) + triple-bond items 0 = 11.
